A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ViMUL and ViMUL-Bench. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original multilingual benchmark results, frame and question-only ablations, controlled CVRR-ES experiments, translation checks and human verification of judge scores.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including model comparisons and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix J retain the same SigLIP encoder, two-layer projector, feature pooling, video/text embedding concatenation and next-token fine-tuning procedure. No algorithmic component or objective is changed.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 14 languages, 15 benchmark domains, training sources and controlled CVRR-ES evaluation. New Appendix O documents domains within existing resources without establishing additional training or evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: The main comparison retains Video-ChatGPT, LLaVA-NeXT-Video, VideoChat2-Mistral, VILA, LLaVA-OneVision and GPT-4o. Comparator membership in the country-information, question-only and frame-input comparisons also remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Established sampling and hyperparameters are retained, but new disclosures are not fully reconciled. Appendix P mentions 130k cycle-consistency translations while Section 4.1 retains 10,000 QA pairs across 10 languages. Appendix R.2 specifies English-first cultural QA creation, whereas Section 3.1 describes native-language creation. The PDFs do not establish whether these reflect changed procedures or inconsistent documentation.

E4.justification: The question-only, single-frame, controlled fine-tuning, location-prompt and video-duration analyses are retained. Translation consistency, judge validation, cultural error analysis and qualitative cases also already appear in v1; the new volunteer instructions do not add analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The demographic clarification about 18 language contributions does not introduce uncertainty estimation or additional experimental repetitions.

E6.justification: Section 5 corrects the reported script-level ranking by adding 'except Chinese' to ViMUL's advantage over open-source models. Figure 5 already shows ViMUL at 49.0% versus LLaVA-OneVision at 53.2% for Chinese in both versions. Numerical results and result entries otherwise remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix J retains the same sampling definitions, embedding dimensions and concatenation equation. No mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: the multilingual cultural video benchmark, approximately 1.2 million training samples and a baseline offering a better high-/low-resource language tradeoff.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly qualifies its correctness criterion as specific to the paper's evaluation setup, limiting its identification with cited evaluation frameworks. Explanations of language gaps, cultural errors and the substantive limitations in Section 7 are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: New Appendices N–P and R substantially expand reproducibility information: artifact licenses, dataset-domain documentation, AMD-MI200 hardware and compute budgets, and detailed collection, annotation, translation-verification and human-scoring instructions. Appendix D explains the 18 language contributions from 16 volunteers. Existing hyperparameters move from Appendix N to Q without alteration.

R1.justification: v2 adds Qureshi et al.'s Thinking Beyond Tokens and removes VURF, HumaniBench and MobiLlama from the references, with corresponding citation edits. Other reference changes include metadata updates for retained works. The central positioning against English-only video benchmarks remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes local wording and cross-reference corrections, condenses the limitations, and adds author contact, equal-contribution and acknowledgement text. Additional appendix sections organize the new documentation, while the main narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Existing displays receive readability refinements, including higher-resolution artwork in Figure 3, reformatted heatmap labels in Figure 5 and redrawn demographic charts in Figure 15. Figures and tables are repositioned during reflow, but the visual evidence and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The added annotation instructions, licensing and compute disclosures make benchmark construction and reuse more auditable. The demographic explanation, Chinese-ranking correction and clearer graphics also improve clarity. These benefits are limited by unresolved inconsistencies in QA creation order and cycle-consistency sample accounting; the underlying empirical evidence remains substantially unchanged.
